Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: The plan provides a comprehensive, district-wide inventory including building ages, sizes, classrooms, portables, and specialized spaces such as science labs, MPR, and athletic fields (p. 155-161). It includes a robust condition assessment of major systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing) with detailed categories and ratings, and connects condition data to facility needs and long-term planning (p. 159-161).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: No detailed enrollment projections or capacity utilization data are provided in the available content. Student population is mentioned only for one site (630 students), with no analysis of trends, capacity, or long-term planning (p. 158).

Educational Alignment.justification: The plan includes detailed educational program needs and priorities from principal interviews, such as specialized rooms for ESL, Speech, Music, Robotics, and Art, and discusses facility needs to support these programs (p. 158). It connects facility projects to educational goals but coverage is partial and focused on specific sites rather than district-wide.

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: The plan references outdoor spaces such as playfields, hardcourts, gardens, and shade structures, but provides minimal detail or district-wide data on greening or shade coverage (p. 158-161). There is no comprehensive strategy for campus greening or outdoor learning.

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: No mention or assessment of climate risks or climate readiness strategies is found in the provided content.

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: The plan mentions some building system upgrades and energy efficiency improvements (e.g., lighting, HVAC), but lacks comprehensive energy data, resilience strategies, or references to state requirements such as Title 24 or Zero Net Energy goals (p. 159-161).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: The plan provides detailed cost summaries for projects with itemized categories and includes a prioritization framework reflecting stakeholder and district priorities (p. 164-166). It identifies funding sources and outlines strategies but lacks comprehensive discussion of long-term financial sustainability or detailed cost estimation methods.
